body:
Accessibility is becoming increasingly important in the publishing industry. Thanks to the opportunities offered by new standards and digital reading technologies a new paradigm is emerging: produce accessible publications and distribute them through traditional distribution channels, so that people with print disabilities can enjoy reading and benefit from the same opportunities and choice as any other reader.
New European and international legislative frameworks are reinforcing the demand for accessible content, not only by encouraging the production of digital accessible books, but also by requiring that the whole value chain (retailers, e-commerce sites, hardware and software, online platforms, DRM solutions, etc.) embrace accessibility. In particular, the recently approved European Accessibility Act invites the entire digital publishing industry to become accessible to disabled and elderly people.
There are already several interest groups working on the implementation of the EU Accessibility Act, but the constitution of the EDRLab membership and the technical expertise of the EDRLab team paves the way for interesting studies on specific topics.
title: Accessibility

body: The Members Circle is a monthly webinar open to all EDRLab members. It is a regular opportunity to meet other members and the EDRLab team.
title: Members Circle

body: Readium is an open-source project that develops toolkits for reading digital publications. EDRLab is one of its main contributors.
title: Readium

body: Readium LCP is a non-proprietary DRM managed by EDRLab. Publishers, distributors and libraries use it to protect and lend publications, and reading applications implement it to open protected content.
title: Readium LCP

body: Thorium Reader is a free desktop reading application created by EDRLab. It reads EPUB publications, including accessible ones with screen reader support, and opens content protected with Readium LCP.
title: Thorium Reader

body: Qualebook is a quality reference framework for digital books, developed with the Standards and Norms working group of the French publishers' association SNE. It covers accessibility, personal data, technical performance and eco-design.
title: Qualebook

body: LINA25, short for Livre Numérique Accessible 2025, is a set of resources in French that helps the French book chain prepare for the European Accessibility Act.
title: LINA25

body: ENACA, for Enhancing Accessibility in Comic Albums, makes digital comics, manga and webtoons accessible with computer vision and language models. The project is led by La Rochelle University (L3i) and Mangas.io. EDRLab contributes through the evolution of EPUB and of the Divina format.
title: ENACA

body: ThinkPub, from 2024 to 2027, is a European project that helps the book sector adapt to digital change through training and an online library of digital learning objects.
title: ThinkPub

body: Radiance is a collaborative project with FeniXX and Isako that studies the use of AI to describe images in scholarly and academic digital publications, with human review. EDRLab contributes its Readium CLI analysis tool and a web component to review and validate the descriptions.
title: Radiance

How to become an EDRLab member

body:
How to Join To become a member of EDRLab, the only requirement is to have an activity in relationship with the object of the Association.
Standard member dues are calculated from their annual gross revenue and size. The current due structure is as follows:
Characteristics of the organization	Member dues (tax excl.) Non-profit organization with budget lower than 2 M€	500 € Company with revenue lower than 2 M€ and less than 20 employees	500 € Non-profit organization with budget larger than 2 M€; Major academic partner member	1000 € Company with revenue between 2 and 10 M€ and less than 50 employees	1000 € Company with revenue between 10 and 50 M€ and less than 250 employees	1800 € Company with revenue larger than 50 M€ or more than 250 employees	3000 € Membership organization with less than 50 members	4000 € Membership organization with more than 50 members	7000 € Major industrial partner member	20000 € Membership becomes effective on the date of payment of the membership dues. Payment options currently include bank transfer, credit card, Paypal or chèque (in France). First year dues are payable at time of application. Online payment EDRLab members can pay their due online via a Credit Card (we are using Stripe).

body:
EDRLab is an international, non-profit development laboratory created in 2015 and based in Paris. Its founding members are Editis, Hachette, Madrigall, Media Participations, the Syndicat national de l'édition, the Cercle de la Librairie, the Centre national du livre, the French State and Cap Digital.
Members elect the Board of Directors. Elected board members serve a two-year mandate, and any member can stand for election. Candidate statements are archived on the EDRLab website. The bylaws are available in English and French.
Members also advise on prospective open-source projects and other undertakings that may be submitted to the membership for approval. Through its W3C membership, EDRLab brings members' needs to the W3C Publishing Working Group.
